description: Blazor WebAssembly client for MentorAgent. Install in your Blazor WASM / Blazor Auto client project. Connects to a MentorAgent.Server hub via SignalR and provides the same ChatWidget experience as Blazor Server.
releaseNotes:
1.0.0-rc.1

		The first release candidate. No new features. This package had no automated coverage before this cycle; it now has a wire-parity suite that parses the hub's SendAsync calls and this client's handlers from source and compares names and arity in both directions, so an event added on one side and forgotten on the other fails the build rather than a support ticket.

		=== Fixed ===================================================================
		- FIXED - IMentorOrchestrator.RespondToApprovalAsync, a public interface member, routed through the RespondToApproval hub method that the server README marks "do not use, deadlocks". SignalR dispatches one hub call at a time per connection, and the turn awaiting approval is holding that slot. The widget never hit it - it goes through IMentorStateService, which was already correct - so every manual test passed; the broken path was a host driving approval from its own UI, on WebAssembly only. It now posts to /mentor/approve. Verified live, cross-origin, on a parked turn.
		- FIXED - CancelCurrentRequest no longer fires a hub call at a dead connection.
		- FIXED - loading MentorAgent.js twice reset the voice state machine and dropped the live SpeechRecognition handle. This is the configuration the documentation recommends here: a standalone WebAssembly app loads index.html before .NET starts, so the script tag goes there, and the widget's HeadContent then injects a second one. Fixed in MentorAgent.Abstractions; upgrade both packages together.
		- The tour URL is resolved against the SERVER's origin, and this is now pinned by a test. Resolving it against the client's origin fetches the WASM app's own index.html and receives it with a 200 - a failure that looks exactly like success.

		=== Known limitations =======================================================
		- A SignalR reconnect is a new connection id, therefore a new server-side DI scope and A NEW CONVERSATION: the previous exchange is gone. That is deliberate - the per-connection scope is what keeps two browsers apart - and it applies with withAutomaticReconnect(), which the documentation recommends. The remedy is to snapshot and restore the session, which brings us to:
		- Session serialize and restore throw NotSupportedException on WebAssembly, naming the reason: the session lives in the server's DI scope. Returning null would have been worse, since null is the documented "no conversation yet", so a host would store nothing every time and never learn why. A server-side snapshot endpoint is a roadmap item.
		- The SignalR hub carries a 32 KB message ceiling, sized from the image options. Oversized arguments abort the connection rather than returning an error.
